problems.description: ~3000 naming violations in new .d.ts declaration files (build.d.ts, cache.d.ts, index.d.ts): snake_case function names, non-PascalCase classes/interfaces, non-UPPER_CASE constants — all contrary to TypeScript/JS conventions (convention score 0.47)

Type declaration files (build.d.ts, cache.d.ts, index.d.ts) appear committed alongside source for a greenfield TS project using gray-matter/marked, which already ship types — suggests generated or redundant declaration files that should be gitignored or removed
package.json dependency ranges are caret-pinned (^15.0.4, ^4.0.3); acceptable since package-lock.json is committed, but exact pins would further harden reproducibility

strengths: Commits package-lock.json (3942 lines) for fully reproducible installs
Proper jest + ts-jest test scaffolding with a dedicated tests/ directory and node testEnvironment
SonarQube deltas all positive: bugs +0, smells -10, cognitive complexity -90, duplications -1.7% — the new code is simple and low-risk
Sensible project layout: TypeScript sources compiling to dist/index.js with a declared bin entry
commit_reviews.summary: Strong greenfield scaffolding (TS + jest, committed lockfile, clean SonarQube metrics), but a 0.47 convention score from ~3000 naming violations in the .d.ts files keeps the commit neutral overall.

problems.description: Handlebars.registerPartial('nav', '') unconditionally registers an empty 'nav' partial, so a template referencing {{> nav}} without a nav.hbs partial silently renders nothing instead of failing.
Inconsistent error handling: resolveTemplate throws on a missing default template while resolveLayout returns null for a missing default layout, making the two resolution paths behave asymmetrically.

Measured convention score (0.47, 3036 violations) is driven by generated .d.ts declaration files (build.d.ts, cache.d.ts, index.d.ts), not by the committed source; the actual new code uses camelCase functions and a PascalCase interface consistent with project style.

strengths: Coherent Handlebars templating layer with standard templates/layouts/partials directory separation, precompiled once in createTemplateEnv for performance
Reuses the existing gray-matter/marked page pipeline and typed Frontmatter object, extending rather than bypassing established patterns
Correctly promotes handlebars from devDependencies to runtime dependencies since build.ts now uses it at runtime
commit_reviews.summary: Adds a well-structured Handlebars templating layer to the static site generator that follows existing module patterns, but the low measured convention score reflects generated .d.ts files rather than the committed code itself.

problems.description: Convention score 0.47 driven by 3036 violations in build.d.ts, cache.d.ts, index.d.ts (PascalCase classes/interfaces, UPPER_CASE constants, snake_case functions). These are generated TypeScript declaration files, so severity is mitigated — but the measurements count them.

Adds two runtime dependencies (chokidar, ws) plus @types/ws for what appears to be a dev-server live-reload feature; if watch/WebSocket is only used in the dev path, chokidar/ws could be devDependencies to keep the published package lean.
No test coverage appears in the diff for the new integration code (+10 functions, +14 imports) beyond the npm dependency updates.
chokidar's transitive deps (anymatch, braces, fsevents, readdirp, etc.) moved out of dev-only, growing runtime install size for watch functionality.

strengths: Uses standard, well-maintained libraries (chokidar for file watching, ws for WebSocket) instead of hand-rolling live-reload plumbing
npm-managed package-lock changes are clean and minimal — no pinned/mutated registry entries
SonarQube delta is uniformly positive: smells -8, cognitive complexity -115, duplications -1.6%, bugs 0
commit_reviews.summary: Coherent integration session adding file-watch + WebSocket live-reload to the SSG with clean dependency management and improved complexity metrics, though the 0.47 convention score is dragged down entirely by naming violations in generated .d.ts build artifacts.

problems.description: The refactor deletes the template/partial/layout rendering path wholesale. build() now only writes a page when page.html is set by a plugin (and index.html only when ctx._renderIndex exists), so if no loaded plugin provides rendering, existing template-based content silently produces no output.

ctx._renderIndex uses a private-by-convention underscore field on the shared plugin context to wire index rendering — a leaked abstraction that creates an implicit contract between the core build loop and a specific plugin instead of a declared interface.

Committed .d.ts artifacts (build.d.ts, cache.d.ts, index.d.ts) account for the bulk of the 3036 convention violations (PascalCase/UPPER_CASE/snake_case rules on generated declarations), dragging the convention score to 0.47.

strengths: Removes two dependencies (marked, handlebars) and ~305 net lines, reducing coupling and the dependency surface.
Plugin lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) provide a clean, ordered extension seam that will scale better than template globbing.
SonarQube metrics improved across the board: -39 cognitive complexity, -4 code smells, -2.1% duplications, +0 bugs.
commit_reviews.summary: Solid architectural refactor with materially better SonarQube health, but the 0.47 convention score reflects violations confined to generated .d.ts files rather than the hand-written source (which follows conventions cleanly) — a discrepancy between the mechanical score and the visible code quality.

problems.description: Commits .ssg-cache.json containing absolute machine-specific paths (/tmp/story_ecb7095c6c25/serve-content-*). The cache is non-reproducible, breaks on any other machine or CI, and is a generated artifact that should be gitignored, not versioned.

Convention score 0.47 with 3036 violations surfacing in build.d.ts/cache.d.ts/index.d.ts: snake_case functions, non-PascalCase classes/interfaces, non-UPPER_CASE constants exported from public type declarations.
Cognitive complexity +179 and +6 smells in a single commit (cache invalidation logic) indicate convoluted control flow disproportionate to the feature scope.
Duplication +1.8% introduced, partially via repeated HTML rendering of identical content across cache entries (5 duplicate page pairs).
Cache file path is derived as contentDir/.. rather than a project-managed location, coupling the cache location to content directory layout instead of explicit configuration.

strengths: Content-aware caching via contentHash + templateHash invalidation is a sound design that correctly skips rebuilds for unchanged pages (all 5 page entries hit identical content hashes).
Follows the existing module structure: new cache.ts is a sibling of build.ts/plugin.ts with typed exports and imports from the shared './types' module.
build() now returns BuildStats, extending the public API in a type-safe way consistent with the existing return-style conventions.
commit_reviews.summary: The caching feature itself is sound, but the commit ships worse than baseline by versioning a machine-specific cache artifact with absolute /tmp paths and tripling cognitive complexity at convention score 0.47.

compounding_issues: Session 1 discarded the seed (an unrelated auth-API scaffold) entirely and started fresh, losing any baseline structure — benign here but wasted the seed
Session 3's naive full-rebuild-on-every-file-change dev server created a performance problem that Session 5 had to retrofit with incremental caching rather than designing it in from the start
The dev server logic added in Session 3 (serve.ts, ~137 lines) was later carved out into plugins/devserver.ts in Session 4, meaning Session 3's implementation was short-lived and paid a rewrite cost
Sessions 4-5 both touched build.ts and devserver.ts in overlapping ways, so the refactor and the cache feature were coupled rather than cleanly sequenced
key_decisions: Adopting Handlebars as the template engine with layouts, partials, and frontmatter-driven template/layout overrides (Session 2)
Building a chokidar-based dev server with WebSocket live-reload and path-traversal protection as an integrated feature rather than a separate tool (Session 3)
Refactoring the monolith into a plugin architecture with lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) and an ssg.config.ts plugin loader (Session 4)
Adding a content-addressed incremental build cache (SHA-256 of content + recursive template hash, .ssg-cache.json manifest, BuildStats) and wiring it into both build and devserver (Session 5)
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality steadily improved across all five sessions with no regression. The project progressed through a textbook arc — greenfield build (11 tests), feature addition via templating (23 tests), integration of a dev server with live reload (30 tests), a structural refactor into a plugin system that preserved all 30 green tests, and a cross-cutting incremental-cache feature that grew coverage to 48 tests across 4 suites while reducing rebuild cost. Each session ended with clean TypeScript compilation and passing tests, and Session 5 deliberately built on the plugin architecture and dev server established in Sessions 3-4 rather than reworking them.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, monotonic-improvement story: an SSG built greenfield, then successively templated, integrated with a live-reload dev server, refactored into a plugin architecture, and finished with incremental caching — with the only real friction being the Session 3 naive-rebuild choice that Session 5 had to retroactively optimize.
